Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does the 20 K estimate predict every die location?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It is a lumped estimate under stated power and boundary conditions, not a spatial map.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Steady heat flow needs both a source and a route to a cooler boundary; peak power alone does not define junction temperature. Trace the visual in order: die power; thermal path; ambient boundary. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic check: at 10 W, a 2 K/W path implies about 20 K rise in a lumped steady-state estimate; that estimate excludes local hot spots. Boundary: The 10 W and 2 K/W values are synthetic classroom numbers.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic check: at 10 W, a 2 K/W path implies about 20 K rise in a lumped steady-state estimate; that estimate excludes local hot spots. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. The 10 W and 2 K/W values are synthetic classroom numbers.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A small contact area or poorly characterized thermal interface can bottleneck an otherwise conductive stack. Trace the visual in order: die; interface contact; spreader / sink. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Compare two synthetic stacks with the same die and sink but different interface contact quality. State what thickness, conductivity, pressure, and voiding data are missing.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Some heat can flow upward through a lid while some flows downward through joints and the board; the shares depend on resistance and boundaries. Trace the visual in order: top path; die source; board path. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Trace both paths for a flip-chip package. If the top sink is removed, predict a redistribution of heat before looking at a model.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
